title: The State of API Clients
tagline: The market that consumes APIs rather than publishing them — why only three of thirty-five publish an API of their own, and why that is a deliberate market movement rather than a measurement failure.

title: The State of Artificial Intelligence APIs
tagline: The AI industry adopted the protocol it invented and none of the safety rails that make it drivable. It shipped the door and skipped the locks.

title: The State of Audience and Measurement APIs
tagline: One of marketing's strongest areas, with an eleven-point buy/sell split inside a single function. The same capability, measured differently depending on who pays for it.

title: The State of Australian Banking APIs
tagline: What fifty Consumer Data Right banks actually publish, scored — and what it means for the operators who run them and the investors who back them.

title: The State of Australian Energy APIs
tagline: What twenty-four Australian energy organizations actually publish, scored — proof that a statutory data mandate transplants from one industry to another, and what it costs to verify one.

title: The State of Australian Healthcare APIs
tagline: What twelve Australian healthcare organizations actually publish, scored — where the challengers out-execute the national agency, and one built the incumbents' FHIR.

title: The State of Australian Insurance APIs
tagline: What twenty Australian insurance organizations actually publish, scored — the country with the machinery for open insurance and no obligation to use it.

title: The State of Australian Payments APIs
tagline: What twenty Australian payment companies actually publish, scored — the NPP-native market where the signature resource is PayID, and the agent surface is almost entirely synthetic.

title: The State of Australian Real Estate APIs
tagline: What eighteen Australian real estate organizations actually publish, scored — the market that mandated the rail instead of the schema, and got an API that carries production traffic.

title: The State of Australian Travel APIs
tagline: What eleven Australian travel and aviation organizations actually publish, scored — the control group, and the lowest contract-quality reading in this entire research programme.

title: The State of API Authentication
tagline: What forty identity, authentication and authorization providers actually publish, scored — the strongest-publishing market in this series, and the one where the scarcest artifact is the thing it sells.

title: The State of Biotechnology APIs
tagline: An industry that built three workflow languages and published zero workflow contracts. Biotechnology solved sequencing, orchestration and reproducibility for compute pipelines over twenty years, and never once pointed that machinery at its own interfaces.

title: The State of Blockchain & Crypto APIs
tagline: One of the highest-publishing large markets in the catalog — median 26.4 against 15.0, idempotency at nearly three times the catalog rate — and OAuth scopes published by 13.3% of its leaders.

title: The State of Canadian Banking APIs
tagline: What 42 Canadian banks, credit unions, caisses, and fintechs actually publish, scored — the emptiest banking market measured, where the rails outrank the banks.

title: The State of Canadian Energy APIs
tagline: What eighteen Canadian energy organizations actually publish, scored — one province mandated Green Button, and the country's best API belongs to a utility nobody compelled.

title: The State of Canadian Healthcare APIs
tagline: What ten Canadian healthcare organizations actually publish, scored — the market with no FHIR-native challenger class, where a practice-management vendor tops the field.

title: The State of Canadian Insurance APIs
tagline: What twenty Canadian insurance organizations actually publish, scored — the only market with a real API certification programme, and its largest carrier is Not Yet Rated.

title: The State of Canadian Payments APIs
tagline: What fourteen Canadian payment companies actually publish, scored — the thinnest, most concentrated market, where the fintechs out-API the incumbents and the rails.

title: The State of Canadian Real Estate APIs
tagline: What fourteen Canadian real estate organizations actually publish, scored — four facets at a clean sweep of zeros, and the fifth consecutive sector in which Canada finishes last.

title: The State of Canadian Travel APIs
tagline: What nine Canadian travel and aviation organizations actually publish, scored — the country that authored the travel industry's flagship standard, and the market where its author is among the worst-published organizations in it.

title: The State of Climate, Energy and Sustainability APIs
tagline: 98% of the upper band publishes a contract — the highest rate measured anywhere — and it is mostly weather APIs. The software that climate regulation created is seventeen companies.

title: The State of Compute & Hardware APIs
tagline: The companies that rent the chips score 36.5. The companies that design and fabricate those same chips score 10.7. NVIDIA scores 24.0 and NVIDIA NIM scores 78.7.

title: The State of Content and Brand APIs
tagline: The lowest governance figure in marketing, in the area whose entire product is an asset other systems depend on retrieving.

title: The State of Conversation and Coaching APIs
tagline: The weakest area in revenue software, and it holds at full coverage. Governance averages 18.1 in the market that holds recordings of every customer conversation.

title: The State of Creator Economy APIs
tagline: The market everyone describes as dependent on platforms turns out to be the one best equipped to survive them.

title: The State of Cybersecurity APIs
tagline: The second-best-scoring market in the catalog — and 72% of it will not tell you how to report a vulnerability, now that the EU Cyber Resilience Act requires exactly that.

title: The State of Data & Analytics APIs
tagline: One of the best-scoring markets in the catalog — and the segment selling "know your data" is the worst-scoring segment inside it, publishing a contract 16.5% of the time against the warehouses' 49.0%.

title: The State of Data and Prospecting APIs
tagline: This area publishes contracts at a higher rate than the market around it and still fails every delegation dimension. The data moves; the permission to act on it does not.

title: The State of Demand Capture APIs
tagline: The second-strongest area in marketing, and the one where the product only works if the handoff works. Programmability here is not a virtue, it is the business model.

title: The State of Developer Tools APIs
tagline: The best-scoring industry in the catalog — first of twenty-five — and it publishes idempotency at the same 2.8% rate as the worst. The gap was never competence.

title: The State of Digital Health APIs
tagline: The market with the best standard and the most mandates publishes consent as a machine-readable surface at 3.4% — the same rate as the rest of the catalog, in the one market built on it.

title: The State of API Documentation
tagline: What twenty-nine documentation platforms, reference renderers and docs-as-code frameworks actually publish, scored — the market whose entire job is making APIs legible, measured on whether its own products are.

title: The State of Earned and Social APIs
tagline: The one area in this report where a low score is partly not the company's fault — and one of only two where the sell side outscores the buy side.

title: The State of Education & EdTech APIs
tagline: The library out-publishes the classroom — scholarly infrastructure publishes a contract 51.0% of the time, corporate learning 0% — and thirty-four organizations in 810 run an MCP server, the lowest of any market scored.

title: The State of Engagement and Outreach APIs
tagline: Sixty-seven percent publish a contract — the highest of any large area in this report. Ninety percent cannot tell an agent whether a call was already made.

title: The State of Gaming APIs
tagline: The product is deliberately closed and the supply chain is wide open. Heroic Labs scores 78.8; Take-Two scores 7.1.

title: The State of Government APIs
tagline: The most consistently contract-publishing market measured anywhere in this research is also one of the least operable. Government did the part the policy named and stopped precisely there.

title: The State of Headless APIs
tagline: What one hundred and six headless CMS, commerce and browser providers actually publish, scored — the architecture whose entire promise is that the API is the product, tested against the evidence, where the monoliths keep the promise better than the disruptors.

title: The State of HR and Workforce APIs
tagline: This market proved it will adopt an API standard when one exists at the right layer. It has done that exactly once, for the narrowest problem in the stack.

title: The State of IoT APIs
tagline: This market solved interoperability where devices meet networks and left it unsolved where customers and agents meet platforms. The best contracts in the research series; the lowest MCP adoption.

title: The State of Legal & Compliance APIs
tagline: The contract lifecycle management segment publishes the fewest contracts in its own market — 18.2% against e-signature's 55.0% — and the market that sells governance scores 9.4 on it.

title: The State of API Management
tagline: What thirty-six API management platforms, gateways and data planes actually publish, scored — the market that sells other people their API practice, measured on its own rubric, where five agentic primitives come back at absolute zero.

title: The State of Market Data APIs
tagline: What the market data providers actually publish, scored — and where the durable value hides in a commoditizing feed.

title: The State of Marketing & Advertising APIs
tagline: The industry whose tracking wrote the world's consent laws describes consent in its own APIs at 4.4% — below the whole-catalog rate, and at zero across the consent-management segment itself.

title: The State of Marketing APIs
tagline: The strongest divide in marketing software is not category, it is customer. Software sold to the advertiser scores 53.3; software sold to the publisher scores 39.0. Both sides run the same real-time auctions against each other. One of them documents how.

title: The State of Mobility APIs
tagline: The best-documented market in this research is the least agent-ready one. Mobility built excellent interfaces for a world of scheduled integrations and webhooks, and that is precisely the investment that does not carry forward.

title: The State of Marketing Orchestration APIs
tagline: The area that automates marketing scores at the marketing average. Orchestration software that cannot itself be orchestrated is the clearest irony in this research.

title: The State of Owned Channel APIs
tagline: The strongest area in marketing, built by companies whose product was always an interface. Even here, delegation is missing at over eighty percent.

title: The State of Paid Media APIs — The Buy Side
tagline: This market transacts entirely by machine and describes itself to the outside world less than almost any other. The bid stream is a specification. The platform is not.

title: The State of Paid Media APIs — The Sell Side
tagline: The lowest scores in either cohort, and the clearest single finding in this research: the side of the transaction with no customer demanding transparency did not build any.

title: The State of Pipeline and Forecast APIs
tagline: This is the most connected software in go-to-market and it sits 1.2 points below the market median on Agent Readiness. Being integrated by everyone is not the same as being operable by anything.

title: The State of Revenue Plumbing APIs
tagline: The best-scoring area in revenue software on every artifact measure, and it fails consent and idempotency at 91% each. Even the market's integration specialists have not built for a caller that acts on someone else's behalf.

title: The State of Quote-to-Cash APIs
tagline: Twenty-three companies, scoring above the market on every artifact measure and failing consent at 96%. The step immediately before money moves is the step least prepared to be delegated.

title: The State of Retention and Advocacy APIs
tagline: The tightest Kin-to-Agent-Readiness gap in either cohort. What these companies publish, an agent can mostly use — there is simply not very much of it.

title: The State of Retention and Expansion APIs
tagline: Twenty companies, and four of the market's own core terms carry no company at all. This is the one area in the report where coverage is a live question.

title: The State of Revenue APIs
tagline: This market has made itself readable by machines and has not made itself operable by them. Fifty-eight percent publish a contract and forty-six percent run their own MCP server, both high figures by any standard in the catalog. Zero describe a workflow. The distance between those two facts is the whole opportunity.

title: The State of Robotics & Autonomous Systems APIs
tagline: This market is not short of APIs — it is short of public ones. 5.8% publish a contract, and the most likely reason is a security posture that treats a documented interface as an attack surface.

title: The State of Space and Aerospace APIs
tagline: Forty years of machine-to-machine standards produced spacecraft that talk to each other across agencies and almost nothing a customer's agent can operate.

title: The State of Supply Chain APIs
tagline: The industry that moves the physical economy publishes idempotency at 1.3% — fifteen companies out of 1,154 — in the one market where a retried request dispatches a second truck.

title: The State of Telecom APIs
tagline: What eighty-three telecom organizations worldwide actually publish, scored — the industry that built a real open standard and then published 351 specifications with no hosts in them.

title: The State of API Testing
tagline: What thirty-seven API testing platforms, mocking tools, load generators, contract frameworks and scanners actually publish, scored — the first market in this series that is genuinely building for agents, and the weakest-scoring one measured.

title: The State of the Sales Handoff APIs
tagline: The area that connects the two cohorts in this research scores like the stronger one. Software defined by a handoff gets good at handing off.

title: The State of UK Banking APIs
tagline: What sixty UK banks and building societies actually publish, scored — from the CMA9 Open Banking mandate to the challengers, building societies, and private banks around it.

title: The State of UK Energy APIs
tagline: What twenty-six UK energy organizations actually publish, scored — the market that mandated the pipes instead of the data, and got exactly what it compelled.

title: The State of UK Healthcare APIs
tagline: What thirteen UK healthcare organizations actually publish, scored — the single-payer market where the incumbent leads and the challengers orbit.

title: The State of UK Insurance APIs
tagline: What thirty-five UK insurance organizations and the London Market actually publish, scored — where a 337-year-old market beat every regulator to open APIs.

title: The State of UK Payments APIs
tagline: What thirty-two UK payment companies actually publish, scored — the open-banking payment-initiation heartland, and the market that hides its own crown jewels.

title: The State of UK Real Estate APIs
tagline: What twenty-four UK real estate organizations actually publish, scored — the market with no MLS, no standard and no mandate, and the best-published real estate sector in the world.

title: The State of UK Travel APIs
tagline: What fourteen UK travel and aviation organizations actually publish, scored — the country that proved mandates work, in the one sector it never mandated.

title: The State of US Banking APIs
tagline: What 113 US banks, credit unions, neobanks, and banking-rails providers actually publish, scored — the one open-finance market with no mandate, and the widest split in banking.

title: The State of US Energy APIs
tagline: What sixty US energy organizations actually publish, scored — the market with the best standard, the largest scale, no obligation, and the lowest average of the four.

title: The State of US Healthcare APIs
tagline: Thirty years of mandated machine-to-machine standards produced clearinghouses, not APIs. The most standardised market measured here is the least programmable one.

title: The State of US Insurance APIs
tagline: What seventy-nine US insurance organizations actually publish, scored — the market with no mandate, where one company in the country publishes bind.

title: The State of US Payments APIs
tagline: What sixty-eight US payment companies actually publish, scored — the deepest, most agent-instrumented payments estate on earth, and the market with no mandate and no floor.

title: The State of US Real Estate APIs
tagline: What forty-five US real estate organizations actually publish, scored — the only industry that successfully mandated a machine-readable contract on itself, and the two points it bought.

title: The State of US Travel APIs
tagline: What thirty US travel and aviation organizations actually publish, scored — the sector where switching cost IS the commercial structure, and the published surface is inversely related to market power.

title: The State of Weather and Geospatial APIs
tagline: The best-governed market in this research scores badly on an instrument built for agents that write. That is a finding about the instrument as much as the market.

title: The State of Where the Spend Lands
tagline: The newest money in marketing arrives on the least described surfaces. Retail media grew into a major channel without building a public interface layer.

title: The Techstars API Portfolio
tagline: Every Techstars company that ships an API, scored the way a machine reads it — a broad accelerator book of clean early-2010s contracts with a thin exemplar ceiling and an unfinished agent story.

title: The A2A Standard
tagline: 65 organizations publish an Agent Card. Ten publish one a conformant client can read. And the ten that got it right score lower on API maturity than the forty-one that got it wrong.

title: The Agent-Era API Standards Onramp
tagline: A sequenced path through the standards a first public API now has to speak — one rung at a time, in order.

title: The API Rating Rubric, Explained
tagline: What the apis.io score measures, why it's weighted the way it is, and how to move it.

title: The Arazzo Standard
tagline: 812 Arazzo documents exist across all of public GitHub. API Evangelist holds 5,276. And the market adopted the specification as a test format, not a description format.

title: The ARD Standard
tagline: Eleven of the largest agent builders specified the discovery layer. Nine companies publish it, seven of them are outsiders, none is fully conformant — and two fail on the specification's own stale documentation.

title: The AsyncAPI Standard
tagline: Across 26,722 providers, exactly one publishes an AsyncAPI document — and 159 describe their events in OpenAPI instead. In its own strongest segment, AsyncAPI is losing 159 to one.

title: The CAMARA Standard
tagline: The industry that standardised itself without being told to — 1,369 participants, 487 organizations, 93 repositories, nothing graduated, and exactly one operator on earth publishing a contract you can call.

title: The GraphQL Standard
tagline: 793 providers publish a GraphQL schema defining 69,521 types — the second-largest description corpus measured here, and the one JSON Schema cannot reach.

title: The JSON Schema Standard
tagline: 9,439,146 schema objects measured inside published API contracts — and an industry still writing with the vocabulary it had in 2013.

title: The List of List Sellers
tagline: The people who email me to sell other people's contact data, recorded as contact data — with the machine-readable file attached.

title: The Model Context Protocol Standard
tagline: 3,060 providers carry an MCP artifact. 672 publish a server you can actually reach. And the median server exposes 11 tools while the largest exposes 588.

title: The OAuth 2.0 Standard
tagline: 775 published contracts still declare the implicit flow — 28.9% of every OAuth-using contract in the corpus, for a flow removed from OAuth 2.1.

title: The OpenAPI Standard
tagline: 14,257 real OpenAPI documents, read as published. One in three carries no callable address, and OAS 3.2.0 reached four of them in ten months.

title: The OpenID Connect Standard
tagline: The identity layer under everything, declared in 102 of 14,195 published API contracts — 0.72%.

title: The OpenAPI Overlay Standard
tagline: 122 stars, 21 contributors, two people writing four fifths of it — and Elastic, MongoDB, Cloudinary and Vercel running it in production. Attention and adoption have come apart.

title: The Pricing of AI APIs
tagline: How the model labs price inference — and what every API provider can learn about pricing their own.

title: The Pricing of Communication APIs
tagline: How SMS, email, and voice APIs are priced — and the pass-through fees the headline rate hides.

title: The Pricing of Payment APIs
tagline: How payment APIs price a slice of value, not a cost of service — the original take-rate model.

title: The State of Spectral in API Pipelines
tagline: What 1,005 real public pipelines reveal about how teams actually govern their APIs — and the blueprint almost none of them have reached.

title: The Y Combinator API Portfolio
tagline: Every Y Combinator company that ships an API, scored the way a machine reads it — and why the batch is agent-native and governance-empty at the same time.
